data.exact_reserve_text: During 2024, gross ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2022 and prior) increased by $99.5m. This was primarily due to poor experience and reserve strengthening in Syndicate 1919's Casualty Division in respect of the US business. On a net basis ultimate claims have increased by $21.3m. On 2020 and prior this gross experience in Casualty is net nil, due to the loss portfolio transfer on the 2020 & prior years of account. However, as there was IBNR strengthening on the 2021 and post underwriting years, these years have seen a net impact.

prior_year_events.event_name: Poor experience and reserve strengthening in US Casualty
prior_year_events.impact_description: Primary driver of increased gross ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2022 and prior); described as poor experience and reserve strengthening in the Syndicate's Casualty Division (US business).

prior_year_events.event_name: Loss Portfolio Transfer (LPT) on 2020 & prior years
prior_year_events.impact_description: Resulted in gross experience in Casualty on 2020 and prior being net nil due to the LPT enacted in December 2022.

prior_year_events.event_name: IBNR strengthening on 2021 and post underwriting years
prior_year_events.impact_description: The report notes IBNR strengthening on 2021 and post years which contributed to a net impact on those years' reserves.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate reported a gross strengthening of prior year reserves in 2024. The technical provisions note records a gross increase in prior year provisions, driven primarily by adverse experience and reserve strengthening in the US Casualty division, with additional IBNR strengthening on 2021 and later years; a loss portfolio transfer (LPT) on 2020 and prior years neutralised gross Casualty exposure for those years. Overall the report shows a modest gross prior year strengthening in the technical provisions reconciliation, while narrative cites larger movements in ultimate estimates for specific prior-year cohorts.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (gross) has been taken from the Technical Provisions reconciliation line 'Change in estimates of prior year provisions' (gross $20,838k = 20.838m). The narrative elsewhere references a different gross measure ('gross ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2022 and prior) increased by $99.5m') and a net increase of $21.3m; these are different metrics (gross ultimate movement vs movement in held prior year provisions vs net after reinsurance). The chosen figure follows the specified requirement to use the movement in prior year provisions (insurance liabilities gross). All monetary values are reported in the report's native currency (USD) and converted to millions; the JSON field names use the original schema naming convention.
